headline: Claude Code's 'don't ask again' is leaking your passwords
summary: Only one thing worth acting on today: the Claude Code permissions you use every day have a real trap — go check yours first.

items.title: Update: the Claude Code permission trap is leaking passwords
items.pitch: That 'don't ask again' you click every day might let Claude Code send your passwords into a public repo. Take two minutes to check your permission list.
why: Security firm apiiro called out 'don't ask again' — 1,122 public GitHub files contain plaintext passwords
If you use Claude Code daily, this is a real account risk
Details are in the original; for now, check yourself assuming the worst
actions: Open Claude Code's permission allowlist and revoke any unnecessary one-click approvals
Run a secret scan on your regular repos to make sure no password files got committed
deep_dive: This isn't a new feature — it's a permissions design trap: one 'don't ask again' can turn into permanent access, so you have to watch it yourself.
Anyone who's handed it a big directory or a repo with secrets in it and clicked one-click approve should check.
The self-check takes about ten minutes; don't wait for an official fix — tightening permissions and scanning for secrets is the safest move.
